description: Independently published external trade expectations, policy reports, and industry commentary on Indian wholesale sugar procurement and market prices covering December 2026 to May 2027.

records.evidence: With 490+ sugar mills operational across Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka entering peak crushing, early harvest reports indicate solid cane sucrose recovery rates averaging 10.95% to 11.20%. Ex-mill wholesale rates are finding strong support around ₹42.80–44.20/kg due to robust year-end institutional confectionary demand and disciplined monthly mill sales release quotas.
records.remarks: Peak crushing commencement balanced by DFPD domestic release mechanism.

records.evidence: Wholesale distribution hubs in Vashi (Navi Mumbai), Kanpur, and Kolkata report steady secondary pipeline sales. Wholesale realization prices for M-30 crystal sugar are trading at ₹44.50–45.90/kg, maintaining a healthy gross margin spread of ₹1.60–1.80/kg over mill gate purchase parity.
records.remarks: Wholesale market tracking secondary distribution spreads.

records.evidence: National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories highlights active diversion of B-heavy molasses and cane juice towards the 20% Ethanol Blending Programme (EBP), with an estimated 4.2 million tonnes of sugar sacrifice. This structural diversion tightens net free-sale sugar availability, nudging mill procurement prices toward ₹43.90/kg during Makar Sankranti sweetmaking demand.
records.remarks: EBP ethanol diversion quota keeping free-sale market supply tight.

records.evidence: Secondary trade inquiries remain brisk in Northern and Eastern markets. With freight rates stabilizing post-monsoon, wholesale selling quotes for Grade M-30 sugar across Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal mandis are trending around ₹45.00–46.20/kg.
records.remarks: Steady wholesale distribution pull supporting retail pack-out margins.

records.evidence: Heightened speculation surrounding the Union Budget recommendation to hike the statutory Sugar Minimum Selling Price (MSP) from ₹31/kg to ₹38–40/kg has created a firm floor for procurement sauda contracts. Mills in Western Maharashtra and Kolhapur are unwilling to discount below ₹44.00/kg as cane FRP payment commitments mount.
records.remarks: Policy expectation of Sugar MSP upward revision setting ex-mill price floors.

records.evidence: Commercial bulk buyers including beverage manufacturers and industrial bakeries are actively booking forward February delivery contracts in anticipation of pre-summer price hardening, maintaining secondary market rates above ₹46.00/kg.
records.remarks: Forward contracting by industrial buyers lifting wholesale prices.

records.evidence: As crushing operations in Karnataka and Southern Maharashtra wind down ahead of the hot summer, overall national mill arrivals taper. Pre-summer bulk procurement for Holi festival celebrations and ice-cream/carbonated soft drink manufacturing provides strong upward momentum to mill gate tenders (₹44.50–45.60/kg).
records.remarks: Crushing closure in southern mills and seasonal pre-summer beverage buying.

records.evidence: Wholesale mandis in North and Central India experience tight pipeline stocks. Re-sellers in Kanpur and Muzaffarnagar are quoting wholesale M-30 at ₹46.50–47.40/kg with sustained merchant turnover.
records.remarks: Mandi stock pipeline replenishment driving wholesale quotes.

records.evidence: Peak summer temperature surges across northern and western states trigger annual peak in liquid beverage, dairy, and squash consumption. Most Maharashtra and Karnataka mills have formally closed their crushing seasons, concentrating active spot sales among well-capitalized cooperative federations and large private groups at ₹44.70–46.10/kg.
records.remarks: Seasonal peak summer demand coupled with post-crushing supply concentration.

records.evidence: Retail and institutional supply chains report accelerated inventory rotation. Secondary sales prices are commanding an average premium of ₹1.90/kg over procurement tenders, averaging ₹47.30/kg across metropolitan consumption centers.
records.remarks: Accelerated secondary inventory turnover during summer peaks.

records.evidence: Complete cessation of cane crushing across all major states shifts the market entirely into warehouse inventory liquidation mode. With national closing stocks closely monitored by DFPD to safeguard domestic food inflation ahead of general monsoon season, mill procurement rates consolidate at ₹45.00–46.60/kg.
records.remarks: Off-season inventory drawdown and government inventory scrutiny.

records.evidence: Spot wholesale prices in Kolkata, Belgaum, and Pune remain elevated as storage carrying costs and finance costs are factored into secondary distributor billings. Bulk institutional trade settles near ₹47.80/kg.
records.remarks: Carrying cost pass-through sustaining wholesale selling spreads.

records.evidence: Joint industry analysis projects steady upward bias in Q1 sugar pricing (procurement range ₹43.20–44.80/kg) as heavy ethanol blending sacrifice offsets peak crushing arrivals.
records.remarks: Quarterly consensus balancing peak crushing volume against ethanol diversion.

records.evidence: Q2 outlook confirms strong commercial pricing corridor (₹44.60–46.20/kg) driven by crushing closure, pre-summer FMCG demand surge, and warehouse stock carrying charges.
records.remarks: Quarterly consensus reflecting post-crushing supply contraction and summer pull.
